recommendation_issues.problem: Folding writing into SheetJS removes write-excel-file (good on the compact lens) but leans harder on a project with no release since v0.20.3 (2024-07-18) and no commit since 2026-02-09. Plan line 741 already names fallbacks for risky packages; this one needs one too, for example read-excel-file 9.3.10 for reading (reads .xlsx only, not .xls), TextDecoder for CSV, write-excel-file for writing. The recommendation text should also say that column widths need write(..., { cellStyles: true }) and that one Vite 8 build of SheetJS is checked, since SheetJS's own Vite demo stops at Vite 7.3.1.

'paket dosyası depoya konur' commits a binary tarball, which the owner's rules allow only as a deliberate, tracked artifact. Since pnpm 10.26 (2025-12-15) the integrity hash of an HTTP tarball dependency is computed and stored in the lockfile (https://pnpm.io/blog/releases/10.26: 'pnpm now computes the integrity hash for HTTP tarball dependencies when fetching them and stores it in the lockfile.'), so installing from https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/xlsx-0.20.3.tgz is already pinned and tamper-evident. Vendoring adds only independence from the CDN during install. Both are valid; the plan should name one on purpose.

'Panel Chrome ve Edge 111, Firefox 114, Safari 16.4 ve üstünde çalışır' promises more than Vite gives: Vite lowers syntax only and adds no polyfills, so any newer API in our code or a library raises the floor. The text should read as a minimum target that is tested on the oldest browser, not a guarantee.

recommendation_tr picks React Router 8 outright while open_questions leaves the router to the owner; the final text should carry one of them. The trade-off to state: React Router now ships a major each year (7.0.0 on 2024-11-22, 8.0.0 on 2026-06-17; v7 keeps security fixes; declarative mode is the smallest surface to migrate), TanStack Router has stayed on 1.x.

Serving the panel from every API copy is compact and holds at this scale, but the recommendation leaves out cache rules (index.html no-cache, hashed assets long-lived) and chunk-load failures after a deploy, which S13-03's dynamic import and S13-07's router make likely, especially during a rolling deploy behind the load balancer. The SPA fallback must also leave missing /assets and /v1 paths as 404. See the miss at line 706.

Vite 8's default floor includes Firefox 114 to 125, which have no Screen Wake Lock (Firefox 126+). The page must check that the API exists and still work without it; the recommendation does not say so.

misses.finding: Nothing says how panel files are cached or what happens after a deploy. Every Vite build gets new hashed chunk names. A hoca whose panel tab is already open then asks for chunks the new build no longer has (lazy routes, and SheetJS if it is loaded by dynamic import as S13-03 proposes), and the click fails. During a rolling deploy behind the load balancer (line 731) an old API copy can also receive a request for a chunk only the new build has. Vite documents both the failure and the fix: listen for vite:preloadError and reload, and send index.html with Cache-Control: no-cache. If the SPA fallback answers every unknown path with index.html, a missing script comes back as HTML instead of a 404.

verdict_reason: No finding in this slice is high severity, and none was refuted or left unverifiable. All 14 findings were re-checked against their cited source and at least one independent primary source: 13 CONFIRMED, 1 CORRECTED (S13-03: column widths need cellStyles: true, the lazy-load quote came from the glob-import section, SheetJS's Vite demo stops at Vite 7.3.1, and SheetJS CE has not released since 2024-07-18). All 17 checked_ok items held against the npm registry, MDN BCD, W3C and vendor pages. Eight misses were found, none high: four medium (chunk errors and cache headers after a deploy, missing lang="tr", list row order for the AKSİS summary, panel sessions on shared lecture PCs) and four low (display time zone, ASCII headers and NFC, QR encoder, no panel sources in Kaynaklar).
